posts.t:
Hello everyone! I just read caps on price again and I noticed one thing. Please confirm that my assumption is correct.

RBR = Successful bull flag of which top becomes demand. DBD = Successful bear flag of which bottom becomes supply. RBD = Failed bull flag of which bottom (FL) becomes supply. DBR= Failed bear flag of which top (FL) becomes demand.
posts.fa:
سلام به همه! تازه دوباره کپ‌های روی قیمت را خواندم و یک چیز متوجه شدم. لطفاً تأیید کنید که فرضم درست است.

RBR = فلگ گاوی موفق که سقفش به تقاضا تبدیل می‌شود. DBD = فلگ خرسی موفق که کفش به عرضه تبدیل می‌شود. RBD = فلگ گاوی ناموفق که کفش (FL) به عرضه تبدیل می‌شود. DBR= فلگ خرسی ناموفق که سقفش (FL) به تقاضا تبدیل می‌شود.

That looks good guys

Remember to attack each exercise with a purpose. Watch how price left each level and how it returned to the level. If a level gets broken, see what price does then and if the level holds where does it go next. It's not just a matter of going through the motions, you have to act like an investigator.

posts.t:
Hi Gian

To understand how to define a SD zone, we must understand what is behind the zone in terms of Order Flow. We expect that the inner boundary of the zone to be the price where remaining stacks of orders are waiting for execution. Since all we have is the chart, we can spot it by a closer look at the candles. There we look where was the last trade before one side overcome the other. Thinking in Order flow terminology, we may suspect that if one side overcome the other, there might be more orders of the winner side which couldent be filled due to less orders of the loosing side.

Understanding this, we can look for this scenario in the chart:

Now, if you understand this, please show me your explained logic of how to mark your zones...
